result:
FINDING: app/auth.py:14 | security | high | `find_user` builds SQL with an f-string from the user-supplied name, which allows SQL injection and login bypass.
FINDING: app/auth.py:5 | security | high | `SECRET_KEY` is hardcoded in source, so anyone with the code can forge tokens.
FINDING: app/files.py:10 | security | high | `export_report` joins the caller-supplied filename into `EXPORT_DIR` without sanitizing, so path traversal can write files outside the exports folder.
FINDING: app/auth.py:21 | security | medium | The username is used as the PBKDF2 salt, so it is predictable and not unique per user. Use a random per-user salt.
FINDING: app/auth.py:34 | security | medium | `sign_token` is an HMAC over the bare `user_id` with no expiry or nonce, so a leaked token is valid forever.
FINDING: app/auth.py:9 | security | low | PBKDF2 uses only 100,000 iterations, below current recommendations of about 600,000 for SHA-256.
FINDING: app/orders.py:13 | logic | high | `apply_discount` uses `>` where the docstring says "$100.00 or more", so an order of exactly 10,000 cents gets no discount. It should be `>=`.
FINDING: app/orders.py:23 | logic | high | Tax is computed on `subtotal` instead of the discounted amount.
FINDING: app/inventory.py:10 | logic | high | The slice end `start + page_size - 1` returns one item too few per page. It should be `start + page_size`.
FINDING: app/orders.py:55 | logic | medium | `place_order` checks stock per line, then reserves separately and ignores `reserve`'s return value. A repeated SKU can pass the check but fail to reserve, and the order is still created with stock only partly reserved.
FINDING: app/orders.py:33 | performance | medium | `dedupe_skus` tests membership against a list, which is O(n²). Use a companion set.
FINDING: app/orders.py:42 | performance | low | `count_by_status` rescans all orders once per status. A single pass with a counter would do.
FINDING: tests/test_orders.py:19 | tests | high | `test_discount_at_threshold` only prints and has no assertion, so it hides the `>` versus `>=` bug.
FINDING: tests/test_orders.py:24 | tests | high | No test covers the discount-then-tax path, because the test's subtotal is below the threshold, so the tax-base bug goes uncaught.
FINDING: tests/test_inventory.py:5 | tests | high | `assert len(page) <= 10` is too loose and passes with the off-by-one that returns 9 items. It should assert exactly 10.
FINDING: tests/test_inventory.py:18 | tests | medium | `test_reserve_success_and_failure` never checks the remaining stock after a successful reserve.
FINDING: tests/test_auth_files.py:12 | tests | medium | `test_find_user` and the login tests use no injection payload, so the SQL injection is untested.
FINDING: tests/test_auth_files.py:17 | tests | medium | `test_sign_token_is_stable` checks only determinism, not the real HMAC value or its use of `SECRET_KEY`.
FINDING: tests/test_auth_files.py:22 | tests | medium | The export/read round trip never tests path traversal such as `../x`.
FINDING: tests/test_inventory.py:10 | tests | low | The last-page test holds only 5 items, so it cannot expose the `page_size - 1` slice bug.
FINDING: tests/test_orders.py:41 | tests | low | `test_place_order_reserves_stock` doesn't verify that the stored order has the correct `total_cents`.

The reviewers read the code but didn't run the tests. One uncertainty: the stock check in `test_reserve_success_and_failure` depends on the seeded `B2` quantity, which the test reviewer couldn't confirm.
